author: show-me state times
title: Brewers and Cardinals address recent tensions after Uribe incident
text:
Christian Yelich said the conflict between the Milwaukee Brewers and St. Louis Cardinals had been “handled” by Wednesday morning, while Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said he saw no need for further incidents in the series finale at American Family Field.
The dispute became public during Tuesday’s 6-0 Brewers win when reliever Abner Uribe gestured toward the Cardinals dugout after a strikeout. Uribe later accused Marmol of signaling for St. Louis pitchers to hit Milwaukee batters during Monday’s series opener. Marmol denied this allegation, saying, “I’m being honest, never in my Minor League career or big league career have I asked somebody to do it. I just think you’re putting real people at risk, like, it’s not worth it. Say what you want, but that’s my take on it.”
According to both teams, the disagreement stemmed from suspicions that one side was stealing signs—a practice considered acceptable if kept within the field of play. Marmol accused Brewers coaches of relaying signs from their dugout during a rally on Memorial Day against pitcher Matthew Liberatore. Yelich finished that inning with a two-run home run.
Yelich said multiple Brewers players and coaches believed Marmol made gestures suggesting retaliation as Yelich came up to bat again in the fourth inning. In-house footage circulated among Milwaukee players appeared to support this claim; however, Marmol described his actions differently: “We felt like they were being pretty demonstrative about relaying from the dugout. I looked over, I said, ‘Hey, don’t do it. Be smart. You’re going to get somebody hurt.’” He explained that his gestures were meant as warnings rather than threats.
A confrontation occurred during batting practice on Tuesday between Marmol and Brewers hitting coach Daniel Vogelbach regarding these gestures and other behavior observed during Monday’s game and pregame activities Tuesday afternoon.
Marmol confirmed an altercation took place but did not name Vogelbach directly: “Teams have these conversations all the time… Usually you just don’t get that type of demonstrative reaction that spurs further questions.” Alec Burleson of the Cardinals commented on Uribe’s celebration: “Just doing it toward the whole dugout is kind of not acceptable.” Yelich also questioned whether such celebrations were necessary: “Obviously, I don’t think [Uribe’s] strikeout celebration is something that we need to be doing… it might have been a little bit over the top.” Trevor Megill added about Uribe, “Young, emotional player… he’s just a charged-up player, and every game means a lot to him.”
